items.title: 63519_Wild Bill Davison oral history interview
items.q: the first recording I made in that country was with Fessor's Big City Band

ctx.x: And, it's what was played at the first Condon's in New York--

Yes - we played the pop songs of the day mostly; we didn't play all the old Dixie Land tunes. And, then, the first recording I made in that country was with Fessor's Big City Band and it was a very successful record; they sold thousands and thousands of these things before another company bought them out and now

they're reissued again. And, it's still selling again. So, then, I went with Pa Pa Bue and stayed almost a year with them and, of course, the money was good but not nearly the kind of money I would have made if I had been on my own. And, I had to turn down some wonderful festival offers because I just couldn't pull out of the band and leave them without a trumpet player; there isn't that many great trumpet players there and ones that are there, they're very good and I mean exceptional; they're busy.
